name: Dydra
tagline: Hosted RDF triple store with SPARQL 1.1, valid-time indexing and an MCP endpoint on every repository.
description: Dydra is a cloud-hosted RDF graph database run by Datagraph GmbH since about 2010. Each account holds repositories that you load with RDF and query over HTTP with SPARQL 1.1, the SPARQL Graph Store Protocol or the Sesame/RDF4J HTTP protocol, and the operator handles scaling, backups and versioning. It is still actively developed: the 2026 user guide (v1.2) covers valid-time indexing for time-windowed 'collated' queries over sample-style data, an RDF replication client, and an MCP endpoint on every repository that lets language models query in SPARQL, GraphQL or a compact notation called score. It suits small teams that want a standards-based triple store without running GraphDB or Virtuoso themselves.

pricing.notes: Basic use is free; production use is licensed and priced per customer.

scale.notes: Multi-tenant service; capacity is managed by the operator rather than configured by users.

strengths: Standards-first: SPARQL 1.1, Graph Store Protocol and the Sesame HTTP API work with existing RDF tooling
Nothing to operate: repositories are created and queried over HTTP
Valid-time indexing returns whole entities per time window in one query
Per-repository MCP endpoint lets LLM agents explore an unfamiliar graph
weaknesses: Small vendor with opaque, quote-based production pricing
Cloud-only: no self-hosted edition for regulated or air-gapped environments
Little public information on performance limits or SLAs
useCases: Publishing RDF datasets with a public SPARQL endpoint
Time-windowed queries over sensor or tick data modelled as RDF
Giving LLM agents structured access to a knowledge graph
